Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2025-12-31_q425earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 27; calculation C19; calculation C11 - Low: The capital expenditure of USD 190 million named for the second half of 2026 plus USD 232 million spent in the first half is below the full-year guidance range; the named projects may be a subset. A project-level capex schedule would close the difference. Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C23 - Low: Several KPI and funding-float values for the half-year 2025 date are not stated in the supplied reports: the floating-rate share, the balances collected on behalf of banks, the euro share of cash and the six-month 2025 factoring amount. The margins and floors of the term loan and revolving facilities are described as ratings-based without figures, and the filing does not say which revolving facility letter carries the dollar or euro commitment. Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14–15, 27; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 162, 171 - Low: The company reports one segment, so no segment revenue, segment adjusted EBITDA or unit schedule exists; revenue by customer location is shown instead and does not sum exactly to the printed total because of rounding. Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 189; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 10 - Low: Debt by seniority beyond the instrument descriptions, maintenance against growth capex, restricted-cash assessment beyond the USD 40 million held in restricted jurisdictions, a standardized FFO measure and the pension obligation are not established in the supplied reports; no missing balance is assumed to be zero. Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 28; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76 - Low: Net Cash Change is not supplied for FY2025, H1 2025 and Q1 2026 because the filing prints activity totals and a cash roll-forward that differ by 1 from each other through rounding, so no single figure supports both; the FY2025 EBITDA bridge and the income before taxes components also differ by 1 and are kept as printed, not plugged. Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 138–140; 6-K_2026-03-31_brightstar-3312026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C09; calculation C17

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Brightstar is a pure-play lottery operator whose long-dated government contracts support steady cash flow, but its largest customer takes 37% of revenue and a controlling shareholder holding 63.28% of the votes can decide payouts, so creditors carry concentration and distribution risk. The July 2025 sale of the gaming and digital business and the Italian Lotto award reshaped the credit within a year: sale proceeds repaid debt and funded a special dividend and repurchase of USD 859 million within USD 1,041 million of shareholder returns in 2025, then the license took USD 2,601 million of upfront cash across 2025 and 2026, with partners funding 38.5% of it. Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 35, 58, 90, 163, 189; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 17; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C06

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern is the durability of the contracts: the revenue-weighted remaining term of the main contracts is more than five years, the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, 15 platform customers and nearly 90 lottery customers diversify the rest, and the debt reduction and covenant-protected distribution limits after the sale reduce the chance of debt-funded payouts. The view would soften if the Scratch & Win license is extended or replaced on similar terms before 2028, or if the 2026 revolving agreement is shown to carry tight payout limits. It would harden if shareholder returns resume above free cash flow after minority distributions, if a license is lost or renewed on worse terms, or if the controlling holder uses its voting power to approve a debt-funded distribution. Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41, 171; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 15

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The company sold its gaming and digital business to a holding company owned by Apollo funds on July 1, 2025 for USD 4.1 billion net of cash transferred, repaid USD 2,936 million of principal during 2025, and returned USD 1,041 million to shareholders in 2025. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Brightstar's credit is solid on business quality but stretched on cash after the Italian Lotto payment: reported net leverage of 4.72x is well above management's 3.24x, and with distributions continuing, creditors depend on free cash flow recovering as license payments end. At June 2026 reported net leverage was 4.72x, or 4.73x pro forma for the July 31, 2026 repurchases and 4.77x pro forma for the dividend payable September 1, 2026; the effect of the July 10, 2026 tax settlement payment is not established. Liquidity and maturities leave room to wait for that recovery, but management's own outlook implies thin second-half free cash flow. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Business quality is strong and gives visibility. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main strength is contract visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts with government lotteries, fees follow wagers and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, so revenue is more predictable than in most consumer businesses and supports tolerance for leverage above 4x on a reported basis. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million against USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028 adds a second strength, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.19x. The main weaknesses are leverage and cash after distributions. Reported net leverage rose to 4.72x after the final Lotto payment, management's lower figure rests on adding back license amortization, and after USD 194 million paid to minority partners the first-half cash left was USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A credible downside begins with the Italian regulator's replacement award for the Scratch & Win license in 2028, or an earlier United States jackpot drought. The first operational break would be lower service revenue at fixed amortization and equipment costs, which cuts reported EBITDA faster than revenue because fees are percentages of wagers and cost is largely fixed. Higher reported leverage and lower cover follow, and distributions to minority partners and shareholders would continue unless cut, so cash after payouts would turn negative and the revolver would fund the gap. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million would absorb a year of that, but the 2028 maturities of USD 798 million then fall due with weaker earnings, which is when refinancing cost or access becomes the issue. Observable triggers are in the monitoring register: reported leverage above its pro forma level, second-half free cash flow below the implied range, and any renewal news. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C07

Scope is whether the seven supplied filings and earnings presentations can support the financial foundation, the business and transaction facts and the fundamental credit assessment, and what remains missing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings support a credit snapshot of Brightstar Lottery to the June 2026 quarter only as a limited-evidence reading: nothing covers the September 2026 quarter and no financing documents were supplied, so covenant headroom and current trading levels cannot be established.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C3

Earnings and leverage can be read from the filings and the three earnings presentations, but the adjusted earnings measure is reconciled only in those presentations, and the latest balance sheet is 128 days older than the as-of date. Debt, cash and revolver availability can be rebuilt from the June 2026 notes, so conclusions should rest on those and carry the stated limitations.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Brightstar's reported net leverage rose to 4.72x at June 2026 from 3.94x at year-end 2025 after the final Italian Lotto license payment, and management's 3.24x measure depends on adding back license amortization, so creditors should anchor on the higher figure.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C06

Cash interest cover on reported EBITDA is 4.19x for the last twelve months, and liquidity of USD 1,742 million is well above the USD 228 million that falls due in 2027, so the pressure point is cash generation after distributions to minority partners rather than refinancing.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C07; calculation C11

### Financial interpretation

Net leverage on reported EBITDA was 3.94x at the end of 2025 and 4.72x at June 2026, while the issuer's adjusted measure moved from 2.44x to 3.24x. The increase comes from net debt rising by USD 1,064 million over the half year as the final Italian Lotto instalment of USD 1,675 million was paid from operating cash flow, with consortium partners contributing USD 650 million of capital; the year-end net debt excluded the USD 1,680 million payable to the Italian regulator, an obligation that consortium partners were to fund in part.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 12; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C10

Most of the distance between the reported and adjusted denominators is the amortization of upfront license fees, which management adds back as non-cash although the cash was paid in advance. It is USD 201 million of the USD 573 million first-half adjusted EBITDA, or 35%, and its share was 20% in 2025 because amortization of the new Italian Lotto license only began in December 2025, so the adjusted measure now excludes a larger charge that already cost cash. Excluding the Lotto payments, operating cash flow was USD 733 million in 2025 and USD 501 million in the first half of 2026.

Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, page 10; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139; calculation C12; calculation C20

Cash interest cover on reported EBITDA improved to 4.19x for the last twelve months from 3.25x in 2025, on higher reported EBITDA and lower cash interest paid, with first-half interest paid at USD 68 million against USD 89 million. Free cash flow excluding the Lotto payment was USD 269 million in the half year, while dividends and buybacks took USD 130 million and distributions to minority partners USD 194 million, so shareholder returns were not covered by cash after minority distributions.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation C07; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15

Liquidity fell to USD 1,742 million from USD 3,036 million as cash dropped to USD 558 million, and 50% of the cash is in euros. No maturity falls due in the rest of 2026, USD 228 million falls due in 2027 and USD 798 million in 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is limited; the drawn revolver of USD 604 million is due in 2031. Floating-rate debt rose to 40% of the total from 36% and 25% at the two previous year-ends, and no interest rate swaps were held at the end of 2025, so interest cost is more sensitive to euro rates.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation C08; calculation C11

Receivable factoring is a funding source outside reported debt: USD 264 million was factored in the first half of 2026 and USD 440 million in 2025, and the balances collected on behalf of banks fell to USD 78 million from USD 149 million. A pause in factoring would lower operating cash flow and raise reported receivables and debt needs, so factoring volumes and the collected-on-behalf balance are worth tracking beside leverage.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 12; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162

The strongest contrary evidence is that cover and liquidity remain adequate, no maturity falls due before 2027, and management reaffirms its full-year outlook and expects free cash flow to rise after the 2025 to 2028 capital expenditure cycle. That view would win if reported net leverage falls back toward the 3.94x of year-end 2025 as the Lotto cash cost drops out of operating cash flow and minority partners keep funding their share; it would lose if the next report shows net debt above USD 3,848 million, the June figure plus the July repurchases and the September dividend, with no earnings growth.

Build the business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for Brightstar Lottery PLC as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the lottery operating model, the 2025 sale of the gaming and digital business, the Italian Lotto award and its funding, ownership and control, capital allocation and dated events through August 2026.

No external sources were used. Document dates are the signature dates the documents state; the three presentations state none.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Brightstar is a pure-play lottery operator whose long-dated government contracts support steady cash flow, but its largest customer takes 37% of revenue and a controlling shareholder holding 63.28% of the votes can decide payouts, so creditors carry concentration and distribution risk.

The July 2025 sale of the gaming and digital business and the Italian Lotto award reshaped the credit within a year: sale proceeds repaid debt and funded a special dividend and repurchase of USD 859 million within USD 1,041 million of shareholder returns in 2025, then the license took USD 2,601 million of upfront cash across 2025 and 2026, with partners funding 38.5% of it.

Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 35, 58, 90, 163, 189; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 17; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C06
### Key findings

- Revenue is contract-based and long-dated but concentrated in two government licenses. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts, and the two Italian licenses that one regulator awards supply 37% of revenue, so a loss or non-renewal there would cut cash flow far more than any single United States contract.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10, 40; calculation C04

- The Scratch & Win license, 19% of revenue, expires in September 2028 and is stated to be non-renewable, so its replacement is decided by a new award whose conditions the law will set. That date falls in the same year as the first large note maturity, so refinancing and license renewal risk coincide.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40

- The Lotto license, effective December 2025 for nine years, is now secured, but its USD 2,601 million upfront cost was paid in cash and amortizes against revenue for years. Partners funded 38.5% of the final installment through a capital increase, which limits the group's own cash call but means minority holders take a large share of the license's profit.

Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 6-K_2026-03-31_brightstar-3312026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; calculation C02; calculation C05

- Control sits with one shareholder: De Agostini holds 46.29% of the ordinary shares but 63.28% of the votes through the loyalty voting structure, appoints an observer to the board and has executives on it, so payout, financing and merger decisions are effectively its to approve. No sponsor-style willingness evidence exists beyond the documented actions in the registers below, and legal capacity for distributions is not established.

- Capital allocation has tilted toward shareholders: the 2025 special dividend and accelerated repurchase alone were USD 859 million, the regular dividend rose from USD 0.20 to USD 0.23 per share, and USD 186 million of the repurchase program remains, while the company states no formal dividend policy. Creditors are protected mainly by contractual limits and the debt reduction that followed the sale, which this analysis cannot size without the financing documents.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 171, 182–183; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C06; calculation C07

- Structure leaves creditors secured by the shares of the Italian operating subsidiary, with the parent, the Dutch holding company and a US co-issuer as issuers and guarantors of different instruments, and consortium partners owning part of the licensed operating companies. Cash held in the joint ventures is shared with minority partners through dividends of USD 163 million in each of the first halves of 2025 and 2026.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 169–171; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Overall sponsor and governance risk is medium: control and payout discretion are high, but disclosure is detailed, eight of thirteen directors are independent, related-party dealings with the controlling holder are small and the outstanding distribution limits are tied to credit ratings.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is the durability of the contracts: the revenue-weighted remaining term of the main contracts is more than five years, the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, 15 platform customers and nearly 90 lottery customers diversify the rest, and the debt reduction and covenant-protected distribution limits after the sale reduce the chance of debt-funded payouts. The view would soften if the Scratch & Win license is extended or replaced on similar terms before 2028, or if the 2026 revolving agreement is shown to carry tight payout limits. It would harden if shareholder returns resume above free cash flow after minority distributions, if a license is lost or renewed on worse terms, or if the controlling holder uses its voting power to approve a debt-funded distribution.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38–41, 171; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 15
### Limitations

- The terms of the revolving credit agreement signed in March 2026 on distributions, guarantor coverage and security are not stated, so the conclusion that shareholder payouts are contractually limited rests on the earlier agreements' terms and may be wrong for today's facilities.
Basis: 6-K_2026-03-31_brightstar-3312026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 13; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 175

- The significant subsidiaries exhibit and the organization chart were not in the supplied text, so ownership percentages below the parent for most operating companies are not established, which limits the conclusion about where creditor collateral and guarantees reach.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48

- Contract-level data such as expiry dates for the largest United States contracts, renewal options and termination compensation are given only as weighted averages, so the durability conclusion is an average and a single large expiry could change it.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41

- The customer behind the 37% share is not named in the passage on concentration; the match to the Italian regulator rests on the two licenses' shares adding to the same figure, an analyst reading that would be wrong if another customer is meant.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 189; calculation C04

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The company sold its gaming and digital business to a holding company owned by Apollo funds on July 1, 2025 for USD 4.1 billion net of cash transferred, repaid USD 2,936 million of principal during 2025, and returned USD 1,041 million to shareholders in 2025. It won the nine-year Italian Lotto license, paid the EUR 2.23 billion fee in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and had partners fund 38.5% of the final installment.

New debt in the period was a EUR 1 billion term loan due 2030 (March 2025), USD 750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due 2033 (December 2025) that refinanced the 6.250% notes due 2027, and new revolving facilities of USD 650 million and EUR 1.0 billion due March 2031 (agreement March 2026, effective April 2026). The 2026 notes were redeemed in September 2025.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Brightstar Lottery PLC as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is business quality, cash generation, liquidity, leverage, refinancing, ownership and financial policy, built on the supplied financial foundation and business analysis, with a qualitative downside path and monitoring triggers.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Brightstar's credit is solid on business quality but stretched on cash after the Italian Lotto payment: reported net leverage of 4.72x is well above management's 3.24x, and with distributions continuing, creditors depend on free cash flow recovering as license payments end.

At June 2026 reported net leverage was 4.72x, or 4.73x pro forma for the July 31, 2026 repurchases and 4.77x pro forma for the dividend payable September 1, 2026; the effect of the July 10, 2026 tax settlement payment is not established. Liquidity and maturities leave room to wait for that recovery, but management's own outlook implies thin second-half free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C07
### Key findings

- Reported leverage is the figure to anchor on, and it has risen. Net debt of USD 3,796 million was 4.72x reported EBITDA at June 2026 against 3.94x at year-end 2025 (4.73x and 4.77x pro forma for the July 31 repurchases and September 1 dividend, with the July 10 tax payment effect not established), because the final Italian Lotto installment was paid in cash. Management's 3.24x adds back USD 201 million of license fee amortization, 35% of first-half adjusted EBITDA, for cash that was paid up front, so creditors should read the higher figure as the working measure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 12; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05

- Business quality is strong and gives visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts with government lotteries, the main contracts have more than five years left on average, and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034. That durability helps support leverage above 4x on a reported basis; it weakens only where one regulator controls the license.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40, 41

- Liquidity and maturities are not the pressure point. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million at June 2026 is 1.70 times the USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028, and nothing is due in the rest of 2026, so a refinancing could wait for the outlook to be proved. The drawn revolver of USD 604 million and 40% floating-rate debt do raise interest sensitivity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C03; calculation C04

- Cash generation after minority distributions and payouts is the weakest link. In the first half free cash flow excluding the Lotto payment was USD 269 million, distributions to minority partners took USD 194 million, leaving USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. Management's outlook implies second-half free cash flow before any distributions of only USD 6 million to USD 31 million, so net debt is unlikely to fall in 2026 without lower payouts or partner funding.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7; calculation C06; calculation C08

- License concentration is the main business risk. The two Italian licenses supply 37% of revenue; the Scratch & Win license, 19% of revenue, expires in September 2028 and is stated to be non-renewable, so its replacement lands in the same year as the first large note maturity. The filings give no renewal timetable or terms.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40; calculation C05

- Control and financial policy are a medium risk. One shareholder holds 63.28% of votes, there is no formal dividend policy and payouts continued during the license payment, but eight of thirteen directors are independent and earlier financing agreements capped payouts by rating level; whether the March 2026 revolving agreement does the same is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 171, 175

- Currency mismatch is a secondary risk. Euro debt is 66% of principal while Italy supplies about 40% of revenue, so a stronger euro raises the dollar value of debt faster than earnings, although half of cash is also in euros.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C09
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that the leverage jump reflects a one-off license payment that partners funded in part, that management reaffirms an adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 1.16 billion to USD 1.19 billion with operating cash flow before license payments near USD 750 million, and that it expects free cash flow above USD 400 million a year after the 2025 to 2028 spending cycle. The view would soften if second-half cash flow beats the implied USD 6 million to USD 31 million, if the Scratch & Win renewal is secured early, or if payouts are cut. It would harden if reported net leverage stays above 4.77x at the next report, if the revolver is drawn to fund distributions, or if the Italian regulator signals a less favorable replacement license.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C07
### Limitations

- The outlook figures are management's and the second-half arithmetic subtracts first-half actuals from full-year ranges, so the conclusion that second-half cash flow will not cover payouts could reverse if working capital unwinds after the first-half timing drag the company describes.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C07

- This is a fundamental view that assigns no rating and compares the issuer only with its own history, because no peer or market data was supplied; the strong assessment of business quality is therefore relative to the issuer's contracts, not to other lottery credits.

- The downside path is qualitative and no stress figures are produced, so how far earnings could fall before liquidity tightens is not sized, and the monitoring thresholds are anchored to current levels, not to covenant tests.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C04
- The currency conclusion uses principal by currency from the maturity table and revenue by customer location from the annual report, which are different bases, so the mismatch is indicative.
Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 189

### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strength is contract visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts with government lotteries, fees follow wagers and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, so revenue is more predictable than in most consumer businesses and supports tolerance for leverage above 4x on a reported basis. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million against USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028 adds a second strength, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.19x.

The main weaknesses are leverage and cash after distributions. Reported net leverage rose to 4.72x after the final Lotto payment, management's lower figure rests on adding back license amortization, and after USD 194 million paid to minority partners the first-half cash left was USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. License concentration, a 63.28% controlling holder and 40% floating-rate debt add to the risk; each is explained in the key findings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C06
### Downside scenario

A credible downside begins with the Italian regulator's replacement award for the Scratch & Win license in 2028, or an earlier United States jackpot drought. The first operational break would be lower service revenue at fixed amortization and equipment costs, which cuts reported EBITDA faster than revenue because fees are percentages of wagers and cost is largely fixed. Higher reported leverage and lower cover follow, and distributions to minority partners and shareholders would continue unless cut, so cash after payouts would turn negative and the revolver would fund the gap. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million would absorb a year of that, but the 2028 maturities of USD 798 million then fall due with weaker earnings, which is when refinancing cost or access becomes the issue. Observable triggers are in the monitoring register: reported leverage above its pro forma level, second-half free cash flow below the implied range, and any renewal news.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C07
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Management reaffirmed its full-year outlook on August 4, 2026: revenue of USD 2.50 billion to USD 2.55 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.16 billion to USD 1.19 billion, capital expenditure of USD 450 million to USD 475 million and operating cash flow of about USD 750 million before license payments. The adjusted EBITDA range implies USD 587 million to USD 617 million in the second half against USD 597 million a year earlier, so the outlook is roughly flat after the first half. Tailwinds are digital growth, cost savings of about USD 100 million by 2028 and the end of license payments; headwinds are higher license amortization, a growth investment of about USD 50 million in 2026 and jackpot volatility.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; calculation C07
